item.title: Iwakuni Castle: Hilltop Keep Above the Nishiki — Guide
item.description: Iwakuni Castle crowns the summit of Mount Yokoyama, high above the Nishiki River and the famous Kintaikyo Bridge in eastern Yamaguchi. Originally built in the early seventeenth century by the Kikkawa lords, it was dismantled soon after under the shogunate’s one-castle-per-domain rule and rebuilt in the twentieth century as the handsome white keep seen today. A cable car climbs the mountain in a few minutes, and from the top the reward is a sweeping panorama: the five arches of the Kintaikyo directly below, the town spreading along the river, and the islands of the Seto Inland Sea beyond.

item.title: Iya Onsen: Riverside Baths Down a Cliff — Guide
item.description: Iya Onsen is one of the most memorable hot springs in Japan, thanks to its extraordinary setting deep in the Iya Valley gorge. From a hotel perched on the clifftop, guests ride a private cable car that descends 170 metres straight down the steep, forested cliff face to reach riverside open-air baths (rotenburo) at the very bottom of the gorge, right beside the rushing Iya River. Soaking in the warm, softly mineral water while surrounded by towering canyon walls, forest and the sound of the river is an unforgettable experience, especially amid fresh green or autumn colour.

item.title: Mount Ikoma: Retro Cable Cars and City Night Views — Guide
item.description: Mount Ikoma, rising on the border between Nara and Osaka, is a fun and nostalgic mountain escape easily reached from either city. It’s climbed by the Ikoma Cable Car, the oldest cable railway in Japan (opened 1918), whose famously quirky cars are shaped like a cat (Mike) and a dog (Bull) — a hit with children. At the top sit the charmingly retro Ikoma Sanjo Amusement Park, one of Japan’s oldest, and the atmospheric Hozanji temple on the slope below.

item.title: Mount Tsukuba: Twin Peaks & Cable Car Views Over the Kanto Plain — Guide
item.description: Mount Tsukuba, despite standing just 877 m tall, is ranked among Japan’s 100 famous mountains, its distinctive twin peaks (male and female summits) rising dramatically from the flat Kanto plain, visible from a striking distance. A cable car and separate ropeway make the summit accessible without a demanding hike, leading to observation points with panoramic views that, on exceptionally clear days, stretch as far as Tokyo Skytree and Mount Fuji. Hiking trails also wind up the mountain for those preferring to climb on foot.

item.title: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route: Cross the Japan Alps by Cable Car & Ropeway — Guide
item.description: The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is a spectacular mountain-crossing transport route through the Northern Japan Alps, linking Toyama and Nagano prefectures via a chain of cable cars, ropeways, a trolleybus and highland buses that together climb over 2,400 metres above sea level. The route passes dramatic alpine scenery, including the famous Snow Corridor walls, and in winter and spring the surrounding slopes around Murodo also offer skiing and snowboarding for visitors wanting to combine alpine transport with time on the mountain itself.

item.title: Mt. Ikoma: Retro Cable Car & Night Views — Nara
item.description: Mount Ikoma straddles the Nara–Osaka border and is reached by Japan’s oldest funicular, whose retro cat- and dog-shaped cars delight families. The summit has a nostalgic amusement park and one of Kansai’s great night-view panoramas over the Osaka plain. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Ikoma, Nara (Nara–Osaka border) Hours Cable car daytime–evening; park seasonal Admission Cable car ~¥370 each way; park rides extra Time needed 2–3 hours Best time Clear evenings for night views What to See Japan’s oldest cable car with novelty cat/dog cars — a hit with kids.

item.title: Mount Oyama Guide: Cable Car, Afuri Shrine & Access
item.description: Rising at the eastern edge of the Tanzawa range, Mount Oyama (1,252 m) has been a place of worship and pilgrimage for centuries — and today it’s one of the most accessible and rewarding half-day mountains near Tokyo.
